claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 6 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And one more important question: **Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means either you live with Alex, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for providing that information.

Based on what you've told me:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you at home (meaning you're responsible for him)

Since Alex is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and you're responsible for him, you meet the basic eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Just one final question to ensure there are no other factors: **Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital or care for an extended period, or living with someone else for any reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex was in care for a bit - it was a couple of months earlier this year. But he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. I need to understand this situation a bit better to assess Alex's eligibility properly.

**Can you tell me more about the care arrangement? Specifically:**
- **How long was Alex in care (how many weeks)?**
- **When did he return home to live with you?**
- **While he was in care, did he spend any regular time at home with you (such as 24 hours or more per week)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He was in care for 7 weeks. He came back home about a month ago. While he was in care, he stayed there full-time - he didn't come home to stay with me during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Just to complete the picture: **During those 7 weeks when Alex was in care, were you claiming Child Benefit for him at that time, or are you looking to make a new claim now that he's back home with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to make a new claim now. I wasn't claiming Child Benefit while he was in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: You meet all the standard eligibility requirements for Child Benefit:
- Alex is 6 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex as he lives with you at home

Regarding the time Alex spent in care: While the rules state that Child Benefit payments might be affected if a child is in care for more than 8 weeks, Alex was only in care for 7 weeks (which is under the threshold). More importantly, since Alex is now back home living with you full-time, and you're making a new claim now, you're in a straightforward situation where you qualify for Child Benefit.

You can proceed with making your claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to be aware of the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but this doesn't affect your eligibility to claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
